title: Dimension shifting for Tor along a free presentation, natural in the second variable
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $0\to K\to F\to M\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] with $F$ a free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $i\ge1$ be an integer. Then for every $R$-module $N$ there is an isomorphism of $R$-modules $\theta_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,N)$, with $\operatorname{Tor}$ and its functoriality in the second variable as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], and these isomorphisms are natural in $N$: for every $R$-linear map $g:N\to N'$ one has $\theta_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,g)=\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,g)\circ\theta_N$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (section-tor) with Lemma Tag 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined, maps of resolutions induce the functoriality) and Lemma Tag 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor); the dimension shift is stated in the proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 ('Since $N^0$ is free, we also see that Tor_2^B(H^0,C)=Tor_1^B(M,C)'); naturality in N: the isomorphism is the connecting map of the long exact Tor sequence in the first variable, which commutes with maps in the second variable

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] to the exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}K\to0\to0$. Its first augmented complex supplies one free resolution $\cdots\to G_2\xrightarrow{e_2}G_1\xrightarrow{e_1}G_0\xrightarrow{\eta}K\to0$. Fix this resolution once for all $N$; in particular the choice does not depend on a map $g:N\to N'$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (section-tor), free resolutions; proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), free-presentation dimension shift

proof.text: Write the given exact sequence as $0\to K\xrightarrow{j}F\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Splice the fixed resolution to it: put $P_0=F$, $P_{n+1}=G_n$ for $n\ge0$, $d_1=j\eta$, $d_{n+1}=e_n$ for $n\ge1$, and augment by $p$. All $P_n$ are free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. This is an exact augmented complex: $\operatorname{im}(j\eta)=j(K)=\ker p$, $\ker(j\eta)=\ker\eta=\operatorname{im}e_1$ since $j$ is injective, and exactness in every higher degree is that of $G_\bullet$. Thus $P_\bullet$ is a free resolution of $M$, also fixed independently of $N$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), free-presentation dimension shift; splicing detail supplied by the agent

proof.text: Compute Tor from these fixed free resolutions [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For $i\ge1$, $P_{i+2}=G_{i+1}$, $P_{i+1}=G_i$, $P_i=G_{i-1}$, and the two differentials around degree $i+1$ in $P_\bullet\otimes_RN$ are exactly $e_{i+1}\otimes1_N$ and $e_i\otimes1_N$. Consequently the identity on $G_i\otimes_RN$ induces an $R$-linear isomorphism $H_{i+1}(P_\bullet\otimes_RN)=\ker(e_i\otimes1_N)/\operatorname{im}(e_{i+1}\otimes1_N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_i(G_\bullet\otimes_RN)$. Compose it with the canonical resolution identifications of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] to define $\theta_N$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (section-tor), Lemma Tag 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined), and proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL)

proof.text: For $g:N\to N'$, the functorial maps of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] on these chosen resolutions come from the chain maps $1_{P_n}\otimes g$ and $1_{G_n}\otimes g$. At the three terms used in Step 3, $P_{i+2}=G_{i+1}$, $P_{i+1}=G_i$, $P_i=G_{i-1}$, so the two chain maps are literally the same maps $1_{G_{i+1}}\otimes g$, $1_{G_i}\otimes g$, $1_{G_{i-1}}\otimes g$. They carry cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, and the identity isomorphism between the two quotient modules in Step 3 therefore commutes with the induced homology maps. The canonical resolution identifications are functorial in $N$ by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], giving $\theta_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,g)=\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,g)\circ\theta_N$.

lean.statement: theorem tor_dimension_shift_natural {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (hS : S.ShortExact) [Module.Free R S.X₂] (i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) : ∃ θ : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} R, (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) (i + 1)).obj S.X₃).obj N) ≅ (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj S.X₁).obj N), ∀ (N N' : ModuleCat.{u} R) (g : N ⟶ N'), ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) (i + 1)).obj S.X₃).map g ≫ (θ N').hom = (θ N).hom ≫ ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj S.X₁).map g
